title: Your projects in order, from the office to the field.
intro: What each part of BuildTrack does and how it's used, in the order the job runs. Everything here works today: if it isn't in the product, it isn't in this guide.
s0.title: Getting started
s0.sub: From the demo to your first project running — no months-long rollout.
s0.step.1.rest: Book a demo or join the beta. We set up your company's workspace and the admin gets an email to set their password.
s0.step.2.rest: The office (admins, finance and warehouse) signs in to the web panel with a username and password. Field staff (workers, supervisors and subcontractors) sign in to the app with a QR code and a PIN you hand them.
s0.step.3.rest: A name and the contract amount are enough. The client, the map location and the cost budget are optional — add them whenever you want.
s0.step.4.bold: Assign people to the project and have them install the app.
s0.step.4.rest: Whoever is assigned sees the project in BuildTrack Field and clocks in from day one. The app is on the App Store for iPhone; Android is on its way.
s0.note: NOTE — AMOUNTS ARE HANDLED IN US DOLLARS (USD).
s1.title: Projects & clients
s1.sub: Every project is one file: contract, changes, money and crew on a single record.
s1.step.1.bold: Load the project with its contract.
s1.step.1.rest: The record brings together the summary, the money, the crew, the punch list, the RFIs and the client portal.
s1.step.2.bold: Log change orders on the record.
s1.step.2.rest: They add or subtract, and the revised contract updates instantly, with its history.
s1.step.3.bold: See the project's money at a glance:
s1.step.3.rest: invoiced, collected, what you're owed and what's been spent against the cost budget.
s1.step.4.rest: Only people assigned to the project see it in their app and can clock in there.
s1.step.5.rest: A directory with their billing details and all their projects; from a client's record you create a project with the client already set.
s1.step.6.bold: Close or delete with a safety lock.
s1.step.6.rest: To close or delete you type the project's name, and a project with records can't be deleted by accident.
s1.gain: Open one record and you know where the project stands and what you're owed — without calling anyone.
s2.title: Line-item budgets
s2.sub: What you planned to spend against what's being spent, line by line.
s2.step.1.bold: Build the budget in line items.
s2.step.1.rest: Each line item has a code, a name and a type: labor, subcontract, materials, machinery & equipment, or general.
s2.step.2.rest: Import line items from a CSV or paste them straight from Excel.
s2.step.3.bold: Spending is deducted on its own.
s2.step.3.rest: Supplier payments, approved expenses, warehouse dispatches and paid payroll come off the project budget with no manual reconciling.
s2.step.4.bold: It warns you before it hurts.
s2.step.4.rest: You see original, revised, spent, balance and committed per line item; a line goes to warning at 85% and to over budget past 100%.
s2.step.5.rest: The cost breakdown across labor, subcontractors, suppliers, warehouse and field expenses, as a PDF or an Excel file.
s2.gain: If a line item is eating the margin, you see it in time to fix it — not when the project closes.
s3.title: Invoicing & collections
s3.sub: Invoice on your letterhead, get it signed and chase what's overdue from one place.
s3.step.1.rest: with automatic yearly numbering, discounts and tax. The PDF carries your logo and details, in the panel's language.
s3.step.2.rest: When you pick the project you see what's left to bill against its contract, and the system won't let you go past the contract plus its changes.
s3.step.3.bold: Change orders go through the admin:
s3.step.3.rest: they stay pending approval and can't be collected until approved.
s3.step.4.rest: through a link that opens on their phone (BT-DOC-16).
s3.step.5.bold: Record every collection, even partial ones.
s3.step.5.rest: The balance updates on its own and what's outstanding is sorted by age: current, 1–30, 31–60 and over 60 days. You can also see it by client.
s3.gain: You know who to collect from today, and every document goes out with your company's face on it.
s4.title: Accounts payable
s4.sub: Who you owe and when it's due, with every payment charged to its project.
s4.step.1.rest: with its due date and photos of the document. Filter by supplier, project, category or status.
s4.step.2.bold: Pay in full or in part.
s4.step.2.rest: Each bill keeps its payment history, and whatever is due in the next 7 days shows up on your dashboard.
s4.step.3.bold: Got it wrong? Void the payment.
s4.step.3.rest: The amount goes back to the project's and the line item's budget, no manual reconciling.
s4.step.4.bold: Logged on the wrong project? Reassign it
s4.step.4.rest: to another active project. You void its payments first; they stay in its history.
s4.step.5.rest: you convert the bill with the supplier's number and the record stays linked.
s4.step.6.rest: come in as bills on their own (BT-DOC-09).
s4.gain: You pay on time, every payment lands on the right project and the budget reflects reality.
s5.title: Field and office expenses
s5.sub: Fuel, freight and supplies, with a receipt and an owner — not in a shoebox.
s5.step.1.bold: Your crew submits the expense from the app
s5.step.1.rest: with a photo or PDF of the receipt, on the project where it was spent.
s5.step.2.rest: approve, send it back to the worker to fix, or reject — one by one or in bulk. Only what's approved uses budget, and each step reaches whoever submitted it as a notification.
s5.step.3.rest: rent, utilities and supplies, with your own categories and a reminder for the ones that repeat every month. That way they don't muddy any project's cost.
s5.step.4.rest: by project, type and period, as a PDF on your letterhead or as an Excel file.
s5.gain: Every expense has a receipt, a project and an approver: no more orphan expenses.
s6.title: QuickBooks Online
s6.sub: Run the job in BuildTrack and the books in QuickBooks, without entering anything twice.
s6.step.1.rest: Intuit asks you to sign in and pick the company; BuildTrack never sees your password.
s6.step.2.rest: clients, projects, suppliers and categories with the ones in QuickBooks — or create them there from here.
s6.step.3.rest: with their attachments, from the cutover date you choose, so nothing you already entered by hand gets duplicated.
s6.step.4.bold: Turn on automatic sending if you want:
s6.step.4.rest: whatever changes or gets deleted here is corrected there. It starts off; nothing goes out until you decide.
s6.step.5.rest: If you turn it on, the payments you record in QuickBooks — checks, transfers, cards and credit memos — show up in BuildTrack on their own.
s6.gain: Your accountant stays in QuickBooks and you stop retyping invoices.
s7.title: Time clock & payroll
s7.sub: Real hours for every person, on every project, ready to pay.
s7.who: WORKERS & SUPERVISORS (CLOCK IN) · SUPERVISORS, FINANCE & ADMINS (APPROVE)
s7.step.1.rest: a pin on the map and a radius from 50 to 5,000 m. Anyone who clocks in outside it is recorded and flagged for review; they're never blocked.
s7.step.2.bold: Everyone clocks in from their phone,
s7.step.2.rest: in and out, with time and location. If they move to another project during the day, the transfer is recorded too.
s7.step.3.rest: The app rejects fake locations, a phone clock set back and impossible jumps between one punch and the next. If someone changes the phone's time, their supervisor gets a notification.
s7.step.4.rest: The supervisor approves, flags or rejects the hours on their projects, one by one or in bulk. Nothing counts toward pay until it's approved.
s7.step.5.rest: Payroll multiplies approved hours by each person's rate, won't let you pay the same shift twice and charges the payment to each project's budget. The hours report and the payments can be exported.
s7.gain: You pay for the work that was done, not what the notebook says — and you know what labor costs on each project.
s8.title: Tools & warehouse
s8.sub: What you own, who has it and what's being used up.
s8.step.1.bold: Register every tool with its code
s8.step.1.rest: and its status: available, assigned, under review, damaged or lost.
s8.step.2.rest: The worker accepts or rejects it in their app, and every move stays in the tool's history.
s8.step.3.rest: stock levels, restocks and counts, with low-stock and out-of-stock alerts.
s8.step.4.rest: with their unit cost and line item: the cost lands on the right budget.
s8.step.5.rest: what hasn't come back, what's been out too long and who has what.
s8.gain: No more “I don't have it”: every tool has a history and every dispatched supply has a project.
s9.title: Subcontractors
s9.sub: Third-party work, with proof before you pay.
s9.step.1.rest: with its agreed amount and due date.
s9.step.2.bold: The subcontractor moves it forward from the app
s9.step.2.rest: and uploads evidence: photos, video or PDF.
s9.step.3.bold: You approve or send it back
s9.step.3.rest: with the evidence and the conversation in front of you. The history can't be edited or deleted.
s9.step.4.rest: and, once approved, goes into accounts payable on its own. When you pay, they get a notification.
s9.gain: You pay for verified work and keep each subcontract's balance in view.
s10.title: Daily log
s10.sub: The record of every day on site, which backs you up when someone says “that never happened.”
s10.step.1.bold: Attendance comes from the time clock.
s10.step.1.rest: One tap brings in the crew that clocked in that day.
s10.step.2.bold: Add the work done, notes and weather.
s10.step.2.rest: In the app the weather is detected from the project's location, and notes can be dictated.
s10.step.3.rest: and review them full-size, one by one.
s10.step.4.rest: It's locked and your client sees it in their portal.
s10.gain: A dated daily record with photos: your backup against claims and the best proof of progress for your client.
s11.title: Punch list
s11.sub: What still needs fixing before handover, numbered and with an owner.
s11.step.1.rest: with its per-project number, up to 5 photos, an assignee and a due date.
s11.step.2.rest: reported, in progress, ready for review and closed. If it isn't right, it bounces back.
s11.step.3.bold: Whoever fixes it marks it ready from the app,
s11.step.3.rest: with evidence photos and a note.
s11.step.4.rest: from their portal, with photos, and confirms closing what they reported. If they don't answer in 7 days, you can close it yourself.
s11.gain: Nothing gets lost between calls and chats, and handover closes with evidence.
s12.title: RFIs
s12.sub: Formal questions to the client, numbered and with the official answer on record.
s12.step.1.rest: While it's a draft only your team sees it; when you send it, it gets its number (RFI #001) and, if you want, a response due date.
s12.step.2.bold: The client answers from their portal,
s12.step.2.rest: with nothing to install and no account. The conversation stays in writing, with dates.
s12.step.3.bold: Close it with the official answer
s12.step.3.rest: and record the cost and schedule impact: estimated amount and days of delay. That impact is internal; the client doesn't see it.
s12.gain: The client's decisions are in writing before the work starts — and with them, the backup to bill the change.
s12.note: NOTE — «YOU TOLD ME OVER WHATSAPP» STOPS BEING AN ARGUMENT: EVERY RFI HAS A NUMBER, A DATE AND AN OFFICIAL ANSWER.
s13.title: Time & materials
s13.sub: Extra work that shows up on site, signed the same day and turned into billing.
s13.who: SUPERVISORS (ON SITE) · FINANCE & ADMINS (IN THE OFFICE)
s13.step.1.bold: Write up the ticket on site
s13.step.1.rest: as soon as the work is done, dated the day it was done.
s13.step.2.bold: Get it signed on the spot:
s13.step.2.rest: the client signs on your own phone or through a link. If they reject it, it goes back to the site to be fixed.
s13.step.3.bold: In the office you turn it into a change order
s13.step.3.rest: and the project's contract goes up, with its entry in the history.
s13.step.4.rest: a signed ticket that keeps aging is money you aren't collecting.
s13.gain: Extras stop being free: what was done gets signed and gets billed.
s14.title: Tasks
s14.sub: Who does what and by when, across all your projects.
s14.step.1.rest: with an assignee, priority, start date and due date.
s14.step.2.rest: to do, in progress, review and done, with comments, attachments and history.
s14.step.3.bold: See them as a list or by week:
s14.gain: First thing Monday you know what's overdue and who's maxed out.
s15.title: Client portal
s15.sub: Your client sees their project without calling you: through a link, no account, nothing to install.
s15.step.1.rest: with a link or a QR code. If you want, protect it with a 6-digit PIN and choose how long it lasts: 30 to 180 days.
s15.step.2.bold: They see what you publish, nothing more:
s15.step.2.rest: the daily log with photos, their punch items and the RFIs. They never see amounts, budgets or internal punch items.
s15.step.3.bold: They answer and report right there:
s15.step.3.rest: they answer RFIs, report punch items with photos and confirm when they're fixed.
s15.step.4.rest: Revoking shuts it off instantly; regenerating kills the old link.
s15.gain: Fewer “how's it going?” calls, and a client who trusts you because they can see it.
s16.title: Client signatures
s16.sub: What was agreed, signed from the client's phone, with proof of what they signed.
s16.step.1.rest: on an invoice, a change order or a time & materials ticket. Send it by email or copy the link; on site, it can also be signed on your phone.
s16.step.2.bold: The client signs with a finger
s16.step.2.rest: on their phone, with no account. The link works once and expires after 14 days.
s16.step.3.rest: name, job title, date, IP address, the signature image and the fingerprint of the exact version of the document.
s16.gain: No more “I never approved that”: every change and every bill carries your client's signature.
s16.note: NOTE — THE DOCUMENT FINGERPRINT (SHA-256) PROVES EXACTLY WHICH VERSION WAS SIGNED.
s17.title: BuildTrack Field app
s17.sub: Your crew's app on site: clock in, report and receive. On the App Store for iPhone; Android is on its way.
s17.step.1.bold: They sign in with a QR code and a PIN
s17.step.1.rest: you generate in the panel: no passwords to forget on site. The app carries your company's logo and speaks Spanish or English.
s17.step.2.rest: clock in and out, see their hours, submit expenses with receipts, accept tools and fix their punch items.
s17.step.3.rest: also run the daily log, the punch list, RFIs, time & materials tickets and expense review.
s17.step.4.rest: move their jobs forward, upload evidence and send their invoices.
s17.step.5.rest: Clock-ins and clock-outs are saved on the phone and sent on their own once there's signal with the app open. Photos, the daily log and the rest need a connection.
s17.gain: Your crew reports from wherever they are, and you see it in the panel without chasing anyone.
s18.title: Security & control
s18.sub: Everyone sees their own, and everything leaves a trail.
s18.step.1.bold: Each role sees only its own.
s18.step.1.rest: Admins, finance, warehouse, supervisors, workers and subcontractors each have their own access, and your company's data is kept apart from every other company's.
s18.step.2.rest: who did what and when, filterable by person, action and date. Nobody can delete it — not even the admin.
s18.step.3.rest: You see each user's active sessions and close them one by one or all at once; deactivating someone removes their access instantly.
s18.step.4.rest: expenses, hours, punch items, RFIs, tools and subcontractors land in the notification inbox of whoever's turn it is.
s18.step.5.rest: Check how each service is doing at any time.
s18.gain: You control who gets in and keep a trail of what they do, without relying on anyone's memory.
